key.text: A small night light for my dorm desk with a warm LED inside and a 3D printed cover. Just one, about the size of my palm.

output.summary: A small 3D printed night light with an LED inside

needs.why: To make the palm-sized cover for the night light
To wire the warm LED inside the light

ways_considered.process: 3D print the cover and assemble the electronics at the bench

routes.process: 3D print the cover and assemble the light using an electronics kit
routes.fit_reason: This route uses beginner-friendly equipment and is open to all students. You can easily make your small night light here.

steps.title: Design the cover
steps.detail: Design a hollow shape that fits in your hand and can hold an LED.

steps.title: Ask staff to check the file
steps.detail: Show your design to the lab staff before printing.

steps.title: Print and assemble
steps.detail: Use the 3D printer for the cover and assemble the LED inside.

warnings.issue: The printed cover might be too thick to let the light shine through.
warnings.fix: Keep the walls thin when designing the cover.

routes.process: 3D print the cover on a Prusa printer and solder the LED at the electronics bench
routes.fit_reason: This route provides reliable 3D printers and a dedicated electronics workbench. Staff are available to help you through the orientation.

steps.title: Take the training
steps.detail: Complete the required safety training and orientation for the space.

steps.title: Design the cover
steps.detail: Create a palm-sized model for your night light cover.

steps.title: Print and solder
steps.detail: Print the cover and use the electronics bench to set up the LED.

warnings.issue: Soldering requires care around hot tools.
warnings.fix: Ask staff for guidance if you have never soldered before.
